originality.rationale: The examined 2024 and 2025 versions of the relevant Lanczos work bound eigenvalue separation and nullspace residual separately, while the nearest prior exact two-dimensional nullspace analysis gives marginal spacing laws and inverse-gap cutoffs. Neither supplies the signed joint covariance, the finite-strength strictly negative association, or the nonmonotone conditional gap/error profile. A specialist equivalent formulation cannot be excluded absolutely.
residual_risks: Exact joint statistics may have been derived elsewhere under degenerate perturbation theory, graph diagonal disorder, or spacing-error coupling terminology.

value.rationale: A natural minimal two-component graph lets both relevant quantities in random-diagonal nullspace computation be measured under the same draw. The exact negative-covariance theorem for all admissible amplitudes and an interior reversal in conditional expected spacing give information neither marginal spacing probabilities nor residual bounds provide; this can calibrate joint risk modeling for Krylov nullspace approximation. The model is narrow but motivated and supplies a complete nonlinear conditional law, not a single arbitrary numerical instance.
